corrections.reason: The classic Andemta Amharic term translating Ge'ez 'አኅርው' (swine/pigs) is 'እጔ' (genitive 'የጔ'). Visually, the top horizontal bar of 'ጔ' is clearly present on the page, distinguishing it from 'ኔ'.
Translating 'ውስተ አኅርው' ('into the swine'). Both visually (top bar of 'ጔ') and philologically, the word is 'በእጔዎች' ('into the pigs'), not 'በእኔዎች'.
Translating 'ቦኡ ላእለ አኅርው' ('they entered into the swine'). The glyph is 'ጔ' with its top bar, giving 'በእጔዎች'.
Translating 'እሙንቱ መራዕይ' ('the herd of swine'). Visually and philologically 'የጔውም መንጋ'.
Translating 'ኖሎት' (the swineherds = 'እጔ ጠባቆች'). Visually the glyph has the top bar of 'ጔ'.
Translating 'ወዘበእንተ አኅርው' ('and concerning the swine'). Visually and contextually 'በእጔዎችም'.
Contraction of ከ + አገራቸው is printed as 4th-order 'ካገራቸው' with a shortened right leg.

In this Ge'ez chapter-section rubric ('ዘከመ ፈወሳ ለእንተ ደም ይውኅዛ' = 'How He healed her who had an issue of blood'), the verb carries the 3rd-person feminine singular object suffix ('ፈወሳ'), and visually on the page there is no 'ኒ' character—only 'ፈወሳ'.
